label: NEW PATTERNS

cover.headline: The same argument, again? *5 ways to change the pattern*
cover.sub: You can’t redo the last round, but you can change the next one.

points.heading: Spot the first thirty seconds
points.body: Repeat arguments tend to start the same way. Notice the line or the tone that sets yours off.
points.panel: Finish this sentence: “It always starts when…”

points.heading: Call a pause before it peaks
points.body: A break isn’t walking away if you say when you’ll come back.
points.panel: “I want to get this right. Can we take twenty minutes?”

points.heading: Trade “always” for “this time”
points.body: “You always” starts a trial. “This time” keeps it to one event you can both look at.
points.panel: “This time, I felt left out of the decision.”

points.heading: Ask what it’s really about
points.body: The dishes are rarely about the dishes. Look for the feeling under the topic.
points.panel: “I think this is really about feeling unappreciated.”

points.heading: End with one small agreement
points.body: You don’t have to solve everything tonight. One next step is enough.
points.panel: “What’s one thing we could each do differently next time?”

close.save: Save this for the next time it starts.

caption:
Some arguments come back so often you could recite both parts.

That’s frustrating, and it’s also useful. A pattern you can predict is a pattern you can interrupt. You only need to change one move, and it can be yours.

Save this for the next round, and follow @spotseason for more small steps.
